propositions: An errored pair is scored as a decision flip because parity.py:107 compares decision fields without an errored guard, while the errored side carries a synthetic decision that was never produced by a model.
A single transient runtime error (throttle) on one arm of a paired parity run causes the paired slot to fail criterion (b) as a fabricated decision flip, incorrectly signaling a quality regression.
An errored record with errored=True and valid=True produces a silent fabricated flip with no corroborating signal in validity or error rate, making it undetectable.
The parity report cannot distinguish genuine flips from fabricated flips across different arms because there is no per-pair detail or excluded-pair count in the metrics.
The guard must exclude errored pairs by testing the errored flag, not by membership in the decision vocabulary, because the gold-pair filter at parity.py:105 tests the label, not the decision.
After the fix, errored pairs are excluded from decision_flips, counted into a new errored_pairs metric, and named in the gating-failure string so different arms produce distinct reports.
